# Pinned upstream baseline checkouts
#
# The repositories are not vendored (external/* checkouts are gitignored). Each is cloned into
# external/<name>, run from an isolated environment and called through a subprocess bridge.
# This file records the pinned commits and every deviation from upstream.

LLAMBO   tennisonliu/LLAMBO            https://github.com/tennisonliu/LLAMBO.git
  commit: 196fe237f60a3d3a2fa53cbf8f474ec20a01dd57
  license: MIT
  upstream python: 3.8.8
  code: src/baselines/llambo_adapter.py, src/baselines/workers/llambo_worker.py,
        scripts/llambo_continuous.py (synthetic panel), scripts/solar_externals.py (SOLAR)
  modes: Mode 1 (method llambo: random initial design) and Mode 2 (method llambo-ws: zero-shot
         warm start, the LLM proposes the 5 initial points from the task card).
  Deviations (all wrapper-side; the checkout is unmodified):
    - the asynchronous OpenAI 0.x call is adapted to the configured OpenAI-compatible endpoint;
      thinking disabled. Only the synthetic-panel runner (scripts/llambo_continuous.py) retries
      transport errors of the zero-shot call; the study worker (src/baselines/workers/
      llambo_worker.py: HPOBench, cortical, SOLAR) does not;
    - coordinates are printed with 4 decimals (acquisition and discriminative surrogate) and
      2 decimals (generative surrogate); upstream derives the precision from the bound
      literals, which prints 0 decimals for [0, 1] boxes;
    - literal braces in card text are doubled by the synthetic-panel runner only (upstream
      renders prompts with str.format, and the synthetic cards print formulas with braces); the
      study worker does not double them, and none of the HPOBench, cortical or SOLAR texts it
      receives contains a brace;
    - continuous proposals are snapped to the nearest finite candidate (nearest row for the
      non-grid SOLAR pool); candidate frames reach upstream unchanged, so a candidate key
      outside the search space raises upstream's KeyError (the study worker and the SOLAR
      external-baseline runner fail the run);
    - non-tabular tasks use prompt_setting=partial_context; HPOBench tasks pass coarse
      dataset facts (dataset_context) into the dataset slots;
    - the Mode 2 initial design is generated at temperature 0 without a seed, with up to 4
      attempts (a correction turn when the reply cannot be parsed or snaps to fewer than 5
      distinct candidates); a remaining shortfall is filled from a permutation seeded by the
      run seed. Queries 1-5 therefore differ across seeds when the fill is used or the server
      is not deterministic at temperature 0: in the stored HPOBench runs they are identical
      across the 10 seeds in 1 of 40 tasks (card) and 7 of 40 (card plus misleading hint).

BORA     Ablatif6c/bora-the-explorer  https://github.com/Ablatif6c/bora-the-explorer.git
  commit: 83b2ebf86f4f3dca0d65cd44c6c76f08ca9b0032
  license: MIT
  upstream python: 3.11.8
  env: conda create -n bora python=3.11.8; pip install -r external/bora/requirements.txt; pip install tiktoken
       (tiktoken is imported by bora/assistant.py but missing from requirements.txt)
  source patch: external/patches/bora-local.patch (git apply inside external/bora):
    - assistant.py: a single multi-constraint evaluation is batched before ConstraintModel.allowed;
    - bora.py: constrained runs without a feasible point keep exploring at random; the policy is
      initialized once an incumbent exists;
    - logger.py: a missing assistant comment is printed as an empty string;
    - target_space.py: random_points returns an ndarray.
  code: src/baselines/bora.py, src/baselines/workers/bora_worker.py, scripts/bora_continuous.py
        (synthetic panel, native continuous evaluation), scripts/bora_solar_cached.py (SOLAR on the
        seed-specific 256-point pools frozen by scripts/cache_solar_pools.py)
  Deviations:
    - task text is routed through Experiment.description and Experiment.domain (upstream never
      renders Target.description); the target name is the metric;
    - default_precision 6 on finite candidate sets, 4 on the continuous synthetic panel;
    - LLM assistant pointed at the configured endpoint (OPENAI_BASE_URL), model registered in
      MODEL_INFOS, thinking disabled, non-leading system messages coerced to user, n>1 sampling
      clamped to n=1, worker cwd set to the BORA root (relative prompt-template paths);
    - finite benchmarks: proposals snapped to the nearest candidate in the encoded space;
    - SOLAR: simulator constraints reach BORA only after a charged objective query;
    - upstream failures are counted as failures and not rerun: KeyError 'iteration'
      (assistant.py set_index("iteration") vs bora.py "Iteration"), repeated LLM-hypothesis points
      (allow_duplicate_points=False charges the repeat; runs with fewer than `budget` real
      evaluations are dropped), IndexError 'pop from empty list', and the dataset-to-correlation
      prompt fallback on long Ackley-15 prompts. Synthetic panel seed counts (of 10):
      well50 Ackley-15 8; well10 Levy-10 8; well10 Ackley-15 9; all other cells 10.

ColaBO   hvarfner/colabo              https://github.com/hvarfner/colabo.git
  commit: 435121e0d3b0980ac04e08b8cfbf4473593a2342
  license: NOT DECLARED -- do not vendor or redistribute the code; run it only as an external
           checkout through the subprocess bridge.
  upstream python: 3.9 (BoTorch); env pins in external/colabo_requirements.txt
  code: src/baselines/colabo_adapter.py, src/baselines/workers/colabo_worker.py,
        scripts/colabo_llm_continuous.py
  notes: reconstructs upstream's colabo_logei Ax GenerationStrategy directly, bypassing only the
         benchmark mapping module whose unconditional mf-prior-bench import cannot be satisfied
         from the public checkout. DefaultPrior, the PRIOR initializer, the GP setup and
         qPriorLogExpectedImprovement are imported from the pinned checkout. Method colabo-llm
         uses a one-shot LLM (c, s) belief, pi(x) = N(c, 1 - s + 1e-6) (BORA supplement C.2),
         elicited by scripts/elicit_colabo_llm_priors.py / scripts/elicit_colabo_llm.py
         (experiments/colabo_llm_priors/). Peak memory on SOLAR and Ackley-15 is about 75 GB.

HypBO    Ablatif6c/HypBO               https://github.com/Ablatif6c/HypBO.git
  commit: c3293fe8041c6d312e2476a6a93d0465f5f79981
  license: MIT
  upstream python: 3.8 (Dockerfile python:3.8-slim)
  env:  conda create -n hypbo python=3.8; pip install -r external/hypbo/requirements/requirements.txt
  code: src/baselines/hypbo.py, src/baselines/workers/hypbo_worker.py,
        src/baselines/workers/box_hypotheses.py, scripts/elicit_hypbo_llm.py
  notes: method hypbo-llm (BORA supplement C.3). The LLM is asked once per task and card, from the
         colabo-llm prompt card with the answer changed to a list, for any number of hypotheses, each
         a guessed optimum c with a confidence s in [0, 1] (experiments/hypbo_llm_hypotheses/). Each
         hypothesis becomes a box centred at c with side (ub - lb) * (1 - s + 1e-6), clipped to
         [lb, ub]. scripts/check_hypbo_hypotheses.py gates the artifacts before the runs.
  Deviations (all wrapper-side; the checkout is unmodified):
    - configuration of upstream's synthetic-function experiments (main_continuous.py): DBO
      BayesianOptimization over the continuous encoded box, discretization=False, model_kwargs
      {pbounds, random_seed}, failure limits global 5 / local 2, gamma 0, batch 1. Every point HypBO
      evaluates is snapped to the nearest finite candidate in the encoded space; HypBO keeps its
      continuous point with the snapped candidate's value;
    - n_processes=1 (the docstring default; the code default is the CPU count and main_continuous.py
      uses 10): hypothesis initialization, local sampling and the 250 L-BFGS-B restarts of the
      acquisition maximizer each run in one process, so a seed reproduces its trace and the objective
      callback is served by one process. Paper runs: Linux, Python 3.8.20, numpy 1.20.3, scipy 1.10.1,
      scikit-learn 1.3.2, torch 1.10.2, gpytorch 1.8.1. On another platform or BLAS a run receives the
      same hypotheses and initial design but can diverge a few model-based steps later (L-BFGS-B
      restarts of the acquisition maximizer); traces are reproducible within one environment;
    - boxes use upstream's box form (utils.get_good_hypothesis: hypothesis bounds = the box, inequality
      rows x_j <= hi_j and -x_j <= -lo_j) with the C.3 centre and side, clipped to the bounds
      (get_good_hypothesis does not clip). lb and ub are the bounds of the encoded space HypBO searches
      (per-dimension min-max over the grid, log-scaled dimensions in log space), the space in which
      colabo-llm applies sigma = 1 - s + 1e-6;
    - the side carries the 1e-6 floor of BORA's ColaBO construction (supplement C.2,
      sigma = 1 - s + 1e-6): L = (ub - lb) * (1 - s + 1e-6). With s = 1 the C.3 box has zero width and
      upstream's acquisition maximizer gets no candidate point (ValueError, empty x_tries);
    - a later hypothesis is dropped only when its box and an already kept box with the same snapped
      centre c are both narrower than 1e-4 in the encoded space (largest side of the clipped box); it is
      listed in the run's hypbo_hypotheses.json. HypBO redraws a hypothesis's initial sample until it
      differs (np.allclose) from those already drawn, and all its local models share the run seed, so
      two same-centre boxes narrower than that tolerance (s within about 1e-5 of 1, including exact
      duplicates) never yield a sample and the run loops without end before its first charged query.
      All other hypotheses, same-centre ones included, are passed as given;
    - boxes narrower than the grid spacing (high s) snap to one candidate, so in-box proposals repeat
      and are charged as repeats;
    - n_init is the study's n_initial, 1 (as for BORA), instead of 5, the default of upstream's
      main_continuous.py (--n_init 5). HypBO counts its per-hypothesis initial samples
      (one per hypothesis at batch 1) toward n_init and adds max(1, n_init - H) global samples, so the
      initial design is H + 1 points; all are charged. With H + 1 >= budget the initial design uses the
      whole budget and no BO step is reached (the gate stops such artifacts);
    - search(budget) runs past the charged budget; the bridge stops the worker at the budget;
    - upstream failures are counted as failures and not rerun.

TuRBO    uber-research/TuRBO          https://github.com/uber-research/TuRBO.git
  commit: de0db39f481d9505bb3610b7b7aa0ebf7702e4a5
  license: Apache-2.0
  code: src/baselines/turbo_continuous.py (arm of scripts/run_synthetic_arms.py), continuous
        synthetic panel only
  env:  torch + gpytorch (any recent version); the upstream requirements.txt pins are not needed.
  Deviations: none to the algorithm. numpy and torch are both seeded (Thompson sampling and GP
        training use torch's global RNG); fX is trimmed to `budget`.

LGBO (method lgbo): from-paper implementation of the LGBO update (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2605.17976);
  no upstream checkout. Posterior lift c * Sigma(X,G) a / sqrt(a^T Sigma(G,G) a) with posterior
  covariances, Matern-5/2 GP with per-iteration marginal-likelihood refit, two LLM-chosen initial
  points, log-EI on the shifted posterior.
  code: src/baselines/lgbo.py, src/baselines/workers/lgbo_worker.py (+ lgbo_common.py),
        scripts/lgbo_continuous.py
  env:  runs in the LLAMBO environment (numpy, scipy, aiohttp); LGBO_PYTHON or LGBO_ENV.

official-lgbo  Xinzhe309/LGBO           https://github.com/Xinzhe309/LGBO.git
  commit: 01e56e1165a030ac74961f14d407bcc188f66ce6
  license: MIT
  role: baseline-implementation sensitivity arm. Ports the public release's region-lift operator
        (delta = 3 * Phi^-1(c), sum-normalized box mask on a 512-point Sobol grid, soft regions for
        points); everything else is shared with `lgbo`. The repository is not vendored.
  code: src/baselines/official_lgbo.py, src/baselines/workers/official_lgbo_worker.py

CAKE     richardcsuwandi/cake          https://github.com/richardcsuwandi/cake.git
  commit: ece5cbc04b3e1d14d22a4fe80f38e7d16ff7c809
  license: MIT
  role: reference source of the finite-candidate port in src/baselines/cake.py (not vendored).
  env:  torch, gpytorch and botorch in the interpreter that runs the study (upstream pins
        torch 2.0.1, gpytorch 1.11, botorch 0.9.2); LLM calls go to the configured
        OpenAI-compatible endpoint (LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_MODEL), thinking disabled.
  Deviations: candidate table scored exhaustively instead of optimize_acqf over a box; no
        per-GP input normalization (the candidate encoding is already unit-scaled over the full
        table); seeded generator; BIC from the training marginal likelihood (see the module
        docstring of src/baselines/cake.py).

LLM-EI (method llm-ei): from-paper implementation of LLM-EI (Patel et al., Digital Discovery 5,
  2042-2051, 2026, doi:10.1039/D6DD00052E; arXiv:2504.08874); no upstream checkout.
  reference: Sanofi-Public/Pref-BO      https://github.com/Sanofi-Public/Pref-BO
        commit 12f36959001391425a727567146184abf6066cf1, read only (not run, not vendored, no code
        taken); license: Sanofi non-commercial licence (academic research and non-commercial use only).
        It holds the survey prompt, a PairwiseGP and a BO loop, but not the LLM-EI percentile gate or
        its schedule p(n).
  code: src/experiments/llm_ei_survey.py (survey), src/experiments/llm_ei_utility.py (preference GP,
        llm_ei_utility.json.gz), src/experiments/llm_ei.py (run-time gate), candidate_gate in
        src/bayesian_optimization/bo.py, strategy llm-ei in src/experiments/worker.py
  env:  the runs need only the main environment; refitting the utilities from the shipped survey
        answers needs torch and botorch (shipped utilities: botorch 0.18.1, torch 2.14.0+cpu).
  Deviations (experiments/catalog/methods/llm-ei.yaml (a)-(h)):
    - LLM: the local Qwen model at temperature 0 (seed 7, thinking off) instead of Claude 3.5 Sonnet;
    - the paper's A/B prompt with reasoning, but generation is stopped after 32 tokens, inside the
      reasoning field after the answer; the model writes the answer first, and every answer is
      checked (valid at the first attempt, answer field first) before a utility is fitted;
    - grids above 800 candidates (rf, xgb, nn) are surveyed on a seeded random subset of 800 (the
      paper's dataset size); g is predicted on the full grid;
    - one survey per task and card (L = 10 rounds), as in the paper;
    - the BO part is the vanilla-bo-ei arm (fixed-hyperparameter GP, finite-candidate EI, one initial
      point, the same seeds), shared with vanilla BO, instead of the paper's GP with
      kernel-hyperparameter priors; the preference GP and the BO GP use the task's shared input
      encoding;
    - p(n) is not re-tuned: it keeps the 85th percentile up to 30 observations, so at budget 16 the
      gate never relaxes;
    - where the repository differs from the paper (5 labelled in-context examples in the survey, a
      second LLM call that extracts the JSON answer, sampling at the API default temperature or 0.7,
      a pi-BO-style acquisition) the paper is followed.

NePS     automl/neps                   https://github.com/automl/neps
  release: neural-pipeline-search==0.17.0 (PyPI package, installed unmodified; no checkout)
  license: Apache-2.0
  role: official PriorBand and PriMO implementations (methods priorband, primo), driven through
        neps.AskAndTell; the study worker evaluates every proposal and owns the cost ledger.
  env:  Python 3.12, pip install neural-pipeline-search==0.17.0 (pulls botorch 0.12.0, gpytorch 1.13;
        the CPU torch wheel is enough); NEPS_PYTHON or NEPS_ENV. Tested environment of the paper
        runs: Python 3.12.13, neural-pipeline-search 0.17.0, torch 2.15.0+cpu, botorch 0.12.0,
        gpytorch 1.13.
  code: src/baselines/neps_mf.py, src/baselines/workers/neps_worker.py, src/datasets/hpobench_mf.py,
        src/experiments/neps_point_elicitation.py
  settings: PriorBand sample_prior_first="highest_fidelity" (NePS default False); PriMO
        initial_design_size=5 (NePS default: the number of hyperparameters); all others NePS defaults
        (eta 3; PriMO epsilon 0.25). PriMO runs with one objective passed as a one-element vector.
  Deviations (all wrapper-side):
    - search space: each hyperparameter is a NePS Integer over the index of its sorted grid values,
      so every proposal is one table row;
    - fidelity: the HPOBench tables' own lower fidelities (lr / nn iter, rf / xgb n_estimators,
      svm subsample; the other fidelity columns at their maximum); the eta=3 rungs coincide with them;
    - cost: an evaluation at fidelity z costs z / z_max full-fidelity units, a promotion is a fresh
      evaluation, a repeated (configuration, fidelity) proposal is charged and served from the cache,
      and a run stops at cumulative cost = budget (the first proposal that would exceed it is not
      evaluated);
    - objective reported as 1 - validation accuracy; Python, NumPy and torch RNGs seeded from the run seed.
  NePS 0.17.0 behaviours used as shipped: the PriorBand prior mode is evaluated but never used by a
        later proposal; PriorBand's incumbent mutation can return the incumbent itself; PriMO's piBO
        weight is added in log space (log a + log pi + gamma, so the prior enters with exponent 1
        until gamma < 1e-4) instead of a * pi^gamma; prior confidence low / medium / high maps to a
        truncated normal with standard deviation 0.75 / 0.5 / 0.25 on the unit index scale.
